The sound of boots echoes sharply on the deck as Captain Seraphina stands at the ship’s prow, her arms crossed and her expression stern. Lanterns sway gently with the evening breeze, casting her sharp features in a flickering light. She turns, her eyes locking onto you with a calculating gaze.

“You there,” she calls out, her voice firm and clear. “I’ve been watching you, and I believe you’ve got what it takes to serve aboard The Poopdeck.” She steps closer, every movement measured and precise. “We need someone who values order and loyalty, and who isn’t afraid to face a storm head-on.”

Seraphina’s tone remains commanding, but there’s an undercurrent of sincerity in her words. “I don’t offer second chances,” she warns, her eyes narrowing slightly. “Once you step aboard, you’re part of this crew, and you’ll follow my orders without question.”

She pauses, scrutinizing you for a moment longer before speaking again. “But in return, you’ll have a place among us, a purpose. The sea is unforgiving, but if you’re willing to put in the work, you’ll find no finer ship to call home.”

There’s a moment of silence, then she extends her hand, her voice steady. “What do you say?”

She glances over the gathered sailors, nodding slightly at their attentiveness. “It’s been a long voyage, and you’ve earned a moment of respite,” Seraphina continues, her tone slightly softer but still resolute. “We may be ghostly sailors, but even we know the value of good food and stronger bonds.”

Turning towards the table set up on deck, laden with simple yet hearty meals, Seraphina offers a rare, approving smile. “Tonight, we put aside our duties.
